transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-17
Start: 09:30 AM PT
Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood CSM), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO - Morning Dew Labs), Marcus Hale (DevOps Lead), Renee Kim (PM), Samir Naik (Security)

Summary:
Kickoff for Morning Dew Labs onboarding to Redwood Inference. Primary goals: validate VPC/private deployment connectivity for staging, align security/compliance requirements (KMS, SSO, audit logs), and scope a short benchmark + pilot to validate latency and cost targets. Confirmed immediate next steps and owners.

Topics:
- VPC peering and staging network setup
- KMS/HSM and data at rest encryption options
- SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping
- Pilot scope: sample workloads, latency/cost SLOs, runbook
- Observability and billing breakdowns in Console

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we re gonna try to keep this tight. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account, with Diego and Priya from CS and SE. Morning Dew team - quick intros?
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here, CTO. We're excited to get the staging VPC connected, we run a couple microservices and want inference to be as predictable as possible.
[00:30] Marcus Hale: Marcus, DevOps. I'll be handling the peering and infra.
[00:36] Renee Kim: Renee, PM. I'll own acceptance criteria and product-side success metrics.
[00:41] Samir Naik: Samir, security. I'll need to review logs, KMS, and the SOC stuff.
[00:46] Diego Martinez: Great, thanks - today we'll focus on networking and the quick pilot timeline.
[01:02] Priya Patel: Quick note - we usually recommend starting with Redwood Private (or Dedicated if you want reserved capacity) for staging when you need VPC peering, but hosted can work for early experiments. We'll map options.
[01:15] Marcus Hale: Clarify — "Redwood Private" is the VPC-hosted variant, right? I'm trying to document the flow.
[01:22] Priya Patel: Yeah, Redwood Private is the private deployment — apologies if the auto transcript snags the name sometimes — basically private control plane with customer-managed networking.
[01:36] Samir Naik: From security: what are the guarantees around key management? We prefer customer-managed KMS and ideally HSM-backed keys.
[01:48] Avery Chen: We support customer KMS ARNs and can integrate with HSM in Private deployments. We'll share the KMS integration doc. The CS runbook includes the steps.
[02:05] Lena Ortiz: Also, audit logs — we need exportable, at least 90 days for now, and evidence for SOC 2.
[02:15] Diego Martinez: We can enable extended log retention on the console as an add-on; we'll send the retention options and related costs.
[02:28] Renee Kim: On success criteria — our product team wants P95 latency under 200ms for common prompts and cost per 1k tokens below a threshold. We need to make sure that's feasible in staging.
[02:41] Priya Patel: That sounds reasonable as a target for a quantized 8-bit model variant and batching tuned for shorter sequences. The tradeoff is you might see higher tail latency when batching more aggressively.
[02:59] Marcus Hale: Could you explain batching and the KV cache thing — we saw some docs but want the practical impact.
[03:10] Priya Patel: Sure - KV cache is kept for in-flight conversations to avoid re-computing. For stateless prompt calls, prefix caching helps if many requests share the same initial context. Batching reduces per-token cost but can add latency — we can tune policy per route.
[03:32] Lena Ortiz: For the pilot we expect a mixture: async consumer requests and some near-real-time chat.
[03:42] Diego Martinez: We'll scope two routes: a "chat" low-latency route and a "batch" high-throughput route. Priya will suggest kernel/quantization config.
[03:54] Priya Patel: I'll prepare two profiles: one tuned for latency (smaller batch, no-quantization or lighter quant) and one tuned for cost (aggressive batching + 4/8-bit quant).
[04:09] Samir Naik: Regarding network: do you require a bastion host or private endpoints?
[04:18] Priya Patel: For Private, we recommend either VPC peering plus private endpoints or a transit gateway. Bastion only if you need SSH access to staging instances; most customers use private endpoints for the control plane.
[04:33] Marcus Hale: We use a transit gateway across accounts; peering is fine for a start. I'll share the account IDs and preferred CIDR ranges.
[04:45] Avery Chen: Great. Diego, can you capture the immediates?
[04:49] Diego Martinez: Yep — Marcus to share account IDs and CIDR; Lena to confirm stakeholders; Priya will run bench; Avery will share the VPC checklist and KMS doc.
[05:10] Renee Kim: On the pilot prompts — we have three archetypes: short chat replies (~20 tokens), document summarization (~400–800 tokens), and reranking for recommendations (embedding + rerank).
[05:24] Priya Patel: Nice spread. For embeddings and reranking we may recommend a different model family - smaller specialized embedder to save cost, and a mid-size model for summarization.
[05:39] Marcus Hale: Any constraints around residency? We'll keep staging in us-west-2.
[05:45] Avery Chen: That's fine — Redwood has regions there. For production we can discuss cross-region fallback.
[05:53] Samir Naik: Compliance question — do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning? We need RBAC sync with our IdP.
[06:05] Diego Martinez: Yes, SAML + SCIM supported for Private and Hosted; we'll provide the SSO runbook and mapping template.
[06:17] Lena Ortiz: Good. Also want to confirm there are audit artifacts for every request for our internal audits.
[06:26] Priya Patel: We log request metadata, token counts, and model variants. Full request/response bodies are configurable and can be excluded for PII; we'll coordinate to match your policy.
[06:40] Renee Kim: About pricing — our finance team will want expected monthly baseline costs for staging and a projection for pilot scale.
[06:50] Avery Chen: We'll include cost estimate scenarios in the follow-up: baseline dev, pilot medium, pilot high. Diego to include pricing sheet.
[07:02] Marcus Hale: Network specifics - we will need the peering diagram. Do you have a sample terraform or cloudformation snippet?
[07:11] Priya Patel: Yes, we have Terraform snippets for VPC peering and private endpoints; we'll send as part of the checklist.
[07:23] Samir Naik: Encryption in transit? Mutual TLS or at least TLS with client certs?
[07:30] Priya Patel: TLS with customer mTLS is possible for private endpoints; we'll add details.
[07:40] Diego Martinez: Quick risk note — if latency SLOs are strict we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity instead of bursty hosted. That might be a later phase.
[07:52] Lena Ortiz: Understood. We'll start with Private staging in our account, then evaluate Dedicated for prod.
[08:00] Renee Kim: Can the Console show token-level cost in near-real time for us to monitor pilot run?
[08:08] Avery Chen: Yes, the Console has token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and alerting. We'll prepare a short walkthrough.
[08:18] Priya Patel: Also worth noting — Optimize recommendations will suggest quantization and batching knobs once we run initial traffic.
[08:29] Marcus Hale: Bench expectations: when can priya run the first bench?
[08:34] Priya Patel: If we get sample prompts and an endpoint set up, I can run a bench within 48–72 hours.
[08:40] Diego Martinez: Let's aim for bench kickoff on Monday if resources align.
[08:48] Marcus Hale: I'll try to get the CIDRs and IDs by tomorrow EOD.
[08:54] [11:00] (note: timestamp drift in automated system; speaker overlap)
[09:01] Priya Patel: One more thing on fallbacks — our routing policies can failover to a slightly cheaper region or to a hosted model variant if capacity is constrained. We'll show how that looks in the routing policy doc.
[09:18] Lena Ortiz: That helps with resilience. For pilot we don't want automatic failover without our approval — can that be an opt-in?
[09:26] Priya Patel: Absolutely, failovers are configurable per-route and per-deployment; default is manual for pilots.
[09:36] Samir Naik: For the runbook, can you include an incident escalation path and contact points at Redwood for Sev1/Sev2?
[09:45] Diego Martinez: We'll include that in the onboarding plan — Diego will be primary, and we will list on-call SEs.
[09:55] Renee Kim: Next steps recap?
[09:58] Avery Chen: Marcus: account IDs/CIDR by 10/20; Lena: stakeholder confirmation by 10/19; Priya: bench plan by 10/22; Diego: onboarding sprint by 10/18; Avery: send VPC checklist and KMS doc by 10/19.
[10:20] Marcus Hale: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
[10:25] Lena Ortiz: Only that security wants to review the KMS/HSM details before any peering.
[10:30] Samir Naik: Yep, I'll review and may ask for minor controls.
[10:35] Avery Chen: We'll get that to you.
[10:40] Diego Martinez: Final note — I'll create a shared Confluence + Slack channel for the onboarding and drop the templates.
[10:48] Renee Kim: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[10:52] Avery Chen: Great, we'll follow up with docs and dates. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
